41.notice: Two options are correct as printed: both the Falkland current (off Argentina) and the Canary current (off north-west Africa) are cold currents. B (Falkland), the textbook example, is the answer kept here.

52.notice: No option is strictly correct. Statement 3 is false (India's hotspots are the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, and Sundaland), and statement 1 is also strictly false, because the hotspot concept came from Norman Myers and Conservation International, not the IUCN. Only statement 2 is broadly true, and no '2 only' option is offered. A (1 and 2) is the answer kept here.

62.why: Hand ruling (dispute): in NCERT the Nawab's inability to control the taluqdars follows the 1801 subsidiary alliance; the 1856 annexation was justified by misgovernment. II is true but not the explanation. Pass A argues this.

68.notice: This item is ambiguous as printed. Statement 2 is correct: Gandhi was in Calcutta on 15 August 1947, not at the Delhi celebrations. Statement 1 depends on reading: Mountbatten did announce the date of 15 August (on 4 June 1947), but the formal transfer of power took place at the Constituent Assembly's midnight session. B is the answer kept here.

71.notice: The case that gave primacy to the Chief Justice and the collegium is the Second Judges Case (1993), which is not among the options. S. P. Gupta (1981, the First Judges Case) actually gave primacy to the executive, but it is the only option about appointing judges and is the answer kept here.
